attribution.note: Marcus quotes his own X post in his own Substack and endorses it. These are his words, not someone else's.

semantics.note: The factual part, that Congress has not put anything serious to a vote, is captured correctly. The normative 'only makes sense if' framing is rightly left out. The claim is an observation about the period up to the post date.

contract.note: Reading 'to a vote' as a full-chamber floor vote is a fair, ordinary reading of firm language. Counting committee votes would change the result, because S. 3312 was voted out of committee in July 2024. The contract correctly flags that interpretation decides the result.

evidence.note: CRS report dated June 2025. It is about enactment of broad AI regulation, not floor votes, and it predates the post. Context only.
Secondary record showing no Senate or House votes on S. 3312, which ended at calendar placement. It supports the claim for this one bill only and cannot establish the universal negative.
Committee ordered S. 3312 reported in July 2024. This is relevant only if committee votes counted. Under the floor-vote contract it does not contradict the claim.

reviews.rationale: The support condition needs a reasonably complete review of floor votes, amendments and larger bills through Nov 19, 2025. The packet checks one candidate (S. 3312, no floor votes) plus a CRS report about enactment. Official action histories returned HTTP 403. No floor vote on qualifying safeguards is shown, so the claim is not contradicted. But the universal negative is not established either, so the outcome is unresolved.
